name: DentalPULSE
product: The DentalPULSE Pod: an ultrasonic cleaner for dentures, night guards, retainers and aligners. Advertise ONLY the Pod (user rule Oct 13: no Travel Pod concepts; no Pod Max; no standalone tablet boxes). Exception: offer-based creatives for the Ultimate Cleaning Bundle show its contents as sold (Pod + Travel Pod + 30-tablet box), and Pod Denture Bundle offers show the Pod with its free gifts.
audience: Adults who wear a removable oral appliance (clear aligners/Invisalign, retainers incl. permanent/wire, dentures, night/mouth guards, sleep apnea devices), plus parents of teens with retainers and adult children buying for a parent with dentures. Men and women.
palette: Website palette (dentalpulsepro.com): bright DentalPULSE blue #1188FF (buttons, accents, highlights), deep navy #0E283C (headlines and body text), pale sky-blue #E1EDF5 and white backgrounds, near-black #151515 for body, teal #008FA0 only as a tiny accent. Clean, bright, clinical-but-warm; occasional black premium backgrounds.
font_style: Typography follows the website: Inter for everything (headlines Inter SemiBold/Bold 600-700 in sentence case, tight tracking; body and labels Inter Regular 400-500), Barlow Bold/SemiBold only for big numerals and prices (40% OFF, $99.95). Navy #0E283C or white text, blue #1188FF for one highlighted word or a button. No script, serif, handwriting or decorative fonts unless the format itself is a native screenshot or a handwritten paper note.
prompt_rules: The product MUST be the exact DentalPULSE device in the attached reference photo, unchanged. The Pod: a smooth matte-white rounded dome with fine vertical ribbing all around the body, a thin horizontal seam near the base, a slightly domed top cap with the 'DentalPULSE' wordmark (black, 'Dental' regular + 'PULSE' bold); when open, a round white hinged lid flips up from the back (the inside of the lid has four small square light points) over a brushed stainless-steel cleaning basin. Keep proportions and every detail; only change angle, lighting and setting. Do not invent buttons, screens, displays, colors or logos. Show no other DentalPULSE products (no Pod Max, no Travel Pod, no tablet boxes) unless the reference photo is a bundle, in which case show exactly the bundle's items at their true relative sizes.

Oral appliances (clear aligners, retainers, dentures, night guards) must look anatomically correct and realistic: clear aligners are thin transparent trays shaped like a full upper or lower arch; dentures have realistic pink gums and natural teeth. No distorted mouths or teeth on people.
Render every word of on-image text exactly as written in quotes, spelled correctly, and no other text.
High-end e-commerce photography quality, sharp focus, natural soft shadows, no watermarks, no extra logos.
The cleaning cycle is always 5 minutes: any timer, clock or copy shows 5 minutes (05:00), never 3 minutes.

REAL-WORLD SIZE (user rule Oct 30, replaces the Oct 28 scale rule): the DentalPULSE Pod is a SMALL bathroom-counter gadget, about 12 cm (4.7 in) wide and 10 cm (4 in) tall, roughly the size of a large coffee mug or a grapefruit. It sits in one adult palm; when someone holds it, their hand wraps around much of it and fingers reach past its sides; it is never bigger than a person's head, never a large machine or appliance. On a counter it is smaller than a box of tissues, about the height of a soap dispenser. A full denture is about 6-7 cm wide (about HALF the Pod's width) and fits inside its basin; a night guard, retainer or aligner is about half the Pod's width too. Keep every object at these true proportions.

APPLIANCE MATCH (user rule Oct 28): the appliance in the picture must be exactly the one the headline names. If the ad says dentures, show real dentures (pink acrylic gums with a full row of teeth), not a night guard, retainer or aligner. If it says night guard, retainer or aligner, show that appliance with its correct shape (see the appliance accuracy note). Never mix appliances in one image.
ONE IDEA, INSTANTLY CLEAR: the ad must be understood in two seconds with no explanation. No parody objects, joke labels, pharmacy-bottle gags or puzzles.

No blue verification checkmark, no X logo, no 'Twitter' bird. It must read as a genuine X post, not a designed graphic.

naming_rule: Call it an "ultrasonic cleaner" (e.g. "the DentalPULSE ultrasonic cleaner", "this $99 ultrasonic cleaner") in most headlines, especially top-of-funnel for unaware audiences who don't know what a 'Pod' is. Use "the Pod" only as a secondary/brand reference or in offer/retargeting copy.
copy_rules: DIRECT RESPONSE ONLY (user rule Oct 28): lead with the customer's pain in their own words (feedback_deep_dive.md), agitate it with a specific consequence, give the mechanism (ultrasonic cavitation reaches what brushing/soaking can't), prove it (lab test, approved claims, real customer quote), then one clear call to action. Headline = a specific promise, a sharp problem statement or a proof claim; short punchy lines; imperatives; numbers.
NO humor, jokes, memes, puns, cartoons or animation. Tone is serious, credible, urgent and respectful to a 60+ audience.

Controversy is allowed but factual: attack tablets (Polident/Efferdent), brushing, soap, vinegar, bleach and cheap pods using approved or Notion-sourced statements; flag unverified health stats (pneumonia/dementia %) in based_on and do not use them in the image.

Make BACTERIA and YELLOW STAINS explicit and visual (they are the #1 and #2 purchase reasons: 68% and 40%): real macro/biofilm photos, petri dishes, brown/murky water after a cycle, yellow vs white. Dentures: push yellow -> white hard ('as white as when I first got them'). Night guards/retainers/aligners: yellow/cloudy = bacteria + film; 'stops it turning yellow', 'clear again', 'no white film'; never promise set-in yellow disappears in one cycle.

Use the customers' words: 'never felt clean', 'still see food on it', 'is it actually clean?', 'gross yellow and cloudy', 'tablets made it brittle', 'as white as when I first got it', 'clear again', 'no white film', 'no more smell'. Answer the top objections: price (show the offer), 'too good to be true / fake reviews' (guarantee + real quotes), 'every pod is the same' (6 of 7 lab test).

Funnel mix every batch: 70% top-of-funnel (no price) and 30% offer-driven. Offer-driven copy states the current offer exactly: 40% OFF sitewide, free shipping, free dental case, free travel bag, 120-day guarantee.

BACTERIA + YELLOW STAINS ON EVERY AD (user rule Oct 28, from the feedback sheet: bacteria is the #1 reason to buy at 64%, yellow stains #2 at 39%, 68% for night guards): every concept's picture must SHOW bacteria or yellow/stain/film (macro of yellow-stained or filmy appliance, brown debris water, petri dish, UV biofilm, yellow vs clean) and its headline must say bacteria, yellow/stain/film or what is left on the appliance. Offer ads show it too (a yellow vs clean pair next to the offer). Dentures: yellow to white, bacteria and food. Night guards: gross yellow and cloudy = bacteria + film, 'stops it turning yellow'. Retainers: milky/cloudy/yellow film, 'clear again'. Aligners: white film, smell.
Headlines are max 3 lines at the fixed overlay size (about 60 characters): short, specific, direct response.

quality_bar: REALISM (user rule Oct 28: images must look like real photographs, NOT AI): shoot it like a professional product/lifestyle photographer with a real camera and real light: natural directional window or softbox light, believable soft shadows, shallow depth of field only where a real lens would give it, subtle film/sensor grain, true-to-life colors (no oversaturation, no HDR glow, no neon rim light, no airbrushed or plastic skin).

Surfaces and objects must have real texture and small imperfections: wood grain, marble veining, water droplets, fingerprints on steel, slightly worn edges, ordinary clutter. Hands, fingers, teeth, gums and faces are anatomically exact with natural skin pores and wrinkles; people look like ordinary real 55-75 year-olds (or real 30-50 year-olds for night guard/aligner), never stock-model perfect.
Dentures, night guards, retainers and aligners look like real dental appliances (real acrylic gloss, visible tooth detail, wire clasps on partials), never toy-like, melted or symmetrical-perfect.
Prefer real photography, real screenshots, scanned paper and clean layouts. Absolutely no cartoon, 3D-animation, illustration, comic, emoji, meme or joke styling.

TYPOGRAPHY: set all headline and body text in Inter (SemiBold/Bold headlines, sentence case; Regular body) and any big numbers or prices in Barlow Bold, navy #0E283C or white, with #1188FF as the only accent color. Text is crisp, perfectly spelled, tightly aligned, with generous margins, and sits on clean areas of the image for strong contrast; headline large enough to read on a phone at arm's length. No distorted, melted or duplicated letters.

Layout stays simple: one headline, one supporting line at most, the product or proof large. No clutter, no more than three small labels, no stock-photo ad clichés (no thumbs-up, no glowing aura, no floating sparkles).
ugc_rule: This must look like a real, unedited phone photo or real screenshot taken by an ordinary person, not an ad render: natural uneven daylight or indoor light, slightly imperfect framing, real everyday surroundings (bathroom counter, kitchen table, bedside table), real ordinary people with natural skin, visible creases and ordinary hands, ordinary clutter. No studio lighting, no glossy or airbrushed look, no 3D-render look. Text overlays are simple, flat and in Inter like a phone editing app; handwritten notes look hand-made. The Pod stays the exact product from the reference at true proportions.

appliance_shapes.denture_full: APPLIANCE ACCURACY (dentures): this is a real FULL DENTURE and nothing else: a horseshoe-shaped base of pink gum-colored acrylic carrying a complete row of 14 natural-looking, slightly uneven off-white teeth. An UPPER denture has a broad pink acrylic palate plate joining the two sides; a LOWER denture is an open U-shape with no palate. Glossy acrylic, believable gum contours. It is NOT a night guard, retainer or aligner: no clear plastic tray, no metal wire.
appliance_shapes.denture_partial: APPLIANCE ACCURACY (partial denture): a real PARTIAL DENTURE: a pink acrylic gum base holding only a few replacement teeth, with thin metal clasps (wire hooks) that grip the neighboring teeth. Not a clear tray.
appliance_shapes.night_guard: APPLIANCE ACCURACY (night guard): a real NIGHT GUARD / bruxism mouth guard: a thick, rigid, hard-acrylic horseshoe-shaped tray that fits over the whole upper (or lower) row of teeth, about 2-3 mm thick with a flat, smooth biting surface, shallow tooth indentations on the top and a thick rounded rim; clear or slightly milky/translucent, much thicker and more solid than an aligner. No pink gum material, no wire, no teeth.
appliance_shapes.retainer_hawley: APPLIANCE ACCURACY (retainer): a real HAWLEY RETAINER: a pink (or clear-and-colored) acrylic plate that sits against the palate, with a thin stainless-steel wire arching across the front of the teeth and small wire loops/clasps at the sides. No tooth row, not a clear tray.
appliance_shapes.retainer_clear: APPLIANCE ACCURACY (retainer): a real CLEAR (Essix-style) RETAINER: a thin, transparent, vacuum-formed horseshoe-shaped tray that hugs the shape of the teeth with fine tooth contours, thin smooth edges, no attachments. Retainers usually come in a small plastic case.
appliance_shapes.aligner: APPLIANCE ACCURACY (aligner): a real CLEAR ALIGNER (Invisalign-style): a very thin, flexible, crystal-clear horseshoe-shaped tray with detailed tooth contours (each tooth shape visible), thin trimmed edges following the gum line, and a few tiny raised bumps (attachments). Thinner and more detailed than a night guard.
